  <bpmn:process id="Process_IP" name="IP" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_IP" name="Transaction data request received">

      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_IP_2</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_IP_3</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_IP_4</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="Task_TransmitData" name="Transmit data to INQ">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_IP_3</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_IP_5</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:sendTask>

    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_IP_4" name="Examination negative" sourceRef="Gateway_Outcome_Split" targetRef="Task_RejectRequest">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression>examination negative</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_IP_5" sourceRef="Task_TransmitData" targetRef="EndEvent_DataTransmitted"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_IP_6" sourceRef="Task_RejectRequest" targetRef="EndEvent_Rejected"/>

rules.instruction: When the description has one participant send a request to another participant, which then performs a check on that request and returns a result to the requester depending on the check outcome: Model the requester's sending of the request as a bpmn:sendTask in the requester's pool. Model the responder's check as a bpmn:task in the responder's pool. Model the returned result as a bpmn:receiveTask in the requester's pool. Connect the send task to the check task and the check task to the receive task with message flows across the pools, following the order given in the description. Do not add start events, gateways or end events for the outcome unless the description states them explicitly.
rules.situation: the description has one participant send a request to another participant, which then performs a check on that request and returns a result to the requester depending on the check outcome

rules.instruction: When the description states that a named participant, as the grammatical subject of a sentence, performs an action on an object, for example by transmitting, checking or answering something for another participant: Name the task with that participant as subject, followed by the verb and object the description uses (for example 'Participant checks the object of other participant'). Do not drop the participant from the label, and do not replace the action with a receive label or switch the perspective to the other party's side of the exchange.
rules.situation: the description states that a named participant, as the grammatical subject of a sentence, performs an action on an object, for example by transmitting, checking or answering something for another participant

rules.instruction: When The description states that one actor sends a request to another actor, that the receiving actor examines the request, and that the receiving actor's reply has content that depends on the examination result, such as transmitting data or rejecting the request.: Model the reply as one task in the replying actor's lane, placed after the examination task and labelled with the description's own verb and main object for that reply. Do not model the reply as a receive task or receive event in the requesting actor's lane. Do not split the reply into separate send tasks, one per outcome. Keep the outcome as the content of that single reply, unless the description states the outcome choice as its own decision step, in which case use one exclusive gateway after the examination.
rules.situation: The description states that one actor sends a request to another actor, that the receiving actor examines the request, and that the receiving actor's reply has content that depends on the examination result, such as transmitting data or rejecting the request.

promoted.trigger: The description states that one participant sends a message to another participant, that the receiving participant checks the message, and that the receiving participant's response has content that depends on the check result, such as delivering data or refusing the message.
promoted.instruction: Model the response as one send task in the responding participant's lane, placed after the checking task and labelled with the description's own verb and main object for that response. Do not model the response as a receive task or receive event in the sending participant's lane. Do not split the response into separate send tasks, one per outcome. Keep the outcome as the content of that single response, unless the description states the outcome choice as its own decision step, in which case place one exclusive gateway after the checking task.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-134, written after it improved the model of example 54
